message.content:
I don’t have the ability to make live HTTP requests from here, but I can give you a ready‑to‑use API call that will return exactly what you’re looking for.  
The **Open Meteo** service is free, requires no API key, and gives hourly forecasts for temperature, wind speed, and precipitation probability.

---

## 1. API URL

```text
https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast
```

### Query parameters

| Parameter | Value | Description |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| `latitude` | `37.8651` | Latitude of the location (Yosemite National Park) |
| `longitude` | `-119.5383` | Longitude of the location (negative for West) |
| `hourly` | `temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_probability` | Which hourly variables you want |
| `forecast_days` | `10` | Number of days to forecast (max 16) |
| `timezone` | `auto` | Optional – sets the timezone to the location’s local time |

### Full request

```text
https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=37.8651&longitude=-119.5383&hourly=temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_probability&forecast_days=10&timezone=auto
```

---

## 2. How to call it

### Using `curl`

```bash
curl "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=37.8651&longitude=-119.5383&hourly=temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_probability&forecast_days=10&timezone=auto"
```

### Using JavaScript (`fetch`)

```js
fetch('https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=37.8651&longitude=-119.5383&hourly=temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_probability&forecast_days=10&timezone=auto')
  .then(r => r.json())
  .then(data => console.log(data));
```

---

## 3. Sample response structure

> **Note:** The numbers below are illustrative; the real API will return the current forecast.

```json
{
  "latitude": 37.8651,
  "longitude": -119.5383,
  "generationtime_ms": 0.45,
  "utc_offset_seconds": 0,
  "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "timezone_abbreviation": "PDT",
  "elevation": 1525.0,
  "hourly_units": {
    "time": "iso8601",
    "temperature_2m": "°C",
    "windspeed_10m": "km/h",
    "precipitation_probability": "%"
  },
  "hourly": {
    "time": [
      "2026-06-20T00:00",
      "2026-06-20T01:00",
      ...
      "2026-07-01T23:00"
    ],
    "temperature_2m": [
      12.3,
      11.8,
      ...
      9.1
    ],
    "windspeed_10m": [
      15.2,
      14.7,
      ...
      12.4
    ],
    "precipitation_probability": [
      0,
      0,
      ...
      20
    ]
  }
}
```

- `time` – ISO‑8601 timestamps in the local timezone.
- `temperature_2m` – Temperature at 2 m above ground (°C).
- `windspeed_10m` – Wind speed at 10 m above ground (km/h).
- `precipitation_probability` – Chance of precipitation (%).

---

## 4. What to do next

1. Copy the full URL into your browser or a terminal.
2. Run the `curl` or `fetch` example to retrieve the JSON.
3. Parse the `hourly` arrays to build your own table or chart for the next 10 days.

If you’d like help turning that JSON into a nicely formatted table or chart, just let me know!
